# Offline test fixtures

These fixtures contain synthetic inputs and reference outputs produced from those
synthetic inputs. They contain no downloaded firmware, vendor model assets,
guitar captures or factory presets.

- `editor-preset.vwm`: synthetic minimal Workbench-format preset named Synthetic.
- `native-body-definition.bin`: generated values across the recovered body schema.
- `native-pickup-definition.bin`: generated electrical/geometry values.
- `native-pack-input.bin`, `native-pack-output.bin`: deterministic synthetic words
  and the original native packer's output for those words.
- `native-resonator-vectors.txt`: finite synthetic boundary values and native outputs.
- `native-body-normalization.txt`: synthetic pickup-position inputs and native float32 results.
- `native-body-interpolation-plans.txt`: synthetic mode/coordinate inputs and traced native routing trees; per-field blending is deliberately bypassed.
- `original-java-word-encoding.txt`: synthetic integer inputs and Java encoder results.

Reference scripts under `scripts/verify_*` document generation and verification.
The ordinary Rust tests use only these fixtures and do not need vendor files or
hardware. Full original-library reference tests require separately obtained local
vendor artifacts and the ignored analysis/tool directories.

- `native-body-interpolation-input.bin`: six generated variants varying all sections, with safe in-memory coil counts and artificial boundary values.
- `native-body-interpolated-cases.txt`, `native-body-interpolated-output.bin`: 84 synthetic routing/direct-blending cases and complete original-machine-code outputs; no vendor bodies are embedded.

- `native-pickup-combinations.txt`: 128 synthetic raw electrical pairings and original-machine-code float64 output bits/active flags, including IEEE arithmetic edge cases.

- `native-pickup-response.txt`: 540 synthetic complex-transfer/primary-fit inputs and exact original-instruction outputs across varied wiring; no vendor definitions.

`native-pickup-biquad.txt` contains 900 synthetic bandpass/float32 response vectors;
`native-pickup-secondary.txt` contains 24 synthetic residual-fit vectors;
`native-pickup-tables.txt` contains 32 complete 64-double tables;
`native-pickup-calculated.txt` contains 16 sets of 83 assigned response fields.
All use synthetic circuit/control data and original instructions with the
initialized v2 private-runtime/host-libm adapters. No bundled definitions, user
presets, or hardware captures are included. See `scripts/verify_pickup_*.py` and
`docs/pickup-response.md` for scope and limits.

Pickup geometry fixtures: `native-body-pole-offsets.txt` (nine synthetic body
outputs), `native-pickup-projection.txt` (120 synthetic inputs and 61 traced setter
values each), and `native-pickup-placement.txt` (48 unique synthetic placements).
`native-pickup-levels-observed.txt` holds 216 electric level/trim cases; the literal
`unobserved` marks the inactive second level, never a fabricated native output.
`native-pickup-tables-wiring.txt` and `native-pickup-calculated-wiring.txt` add
32 tables and 64 calculated responses for varied synthetic loads and rates.
All are generated by the correspondingly named offline verifier scripts.

`native-vx-float.txt` records 1,012 original bit encodings, including arbitrary IEEE
patterns. `native-dsp-scalar.txt` records 297 scalar-setter cases with native changed
words against seeded 1,091-word arrays. Tests reconstruct the whole initial state
and compare every word, including neighbors. Generated by `verify_dsp_scalar.py`.
